claims.rationale: Primary sources refute the minted mechanism: MIGOS's long-cycle-tie value is 0 (thesis §5.3.2; ICGA 2009 §3.3 'typically 0'), identical to our TIE=0; MIGOS's own basic-ko 4×4 = +1 = ours (thesis Table 5.1); the +2 anchor arises from the pass-difference cycle-resolution rule (thesis Appendix A §A.4), a different game definition, not a different tie value. Empirical half (D014 descope, 2026-08-02) confirms the tie constant is a pure value knob on cycle-valued states and inert on resolved ones (2×2/3×2 roots tie-pinned at [−4,4]/[−6,6], V = clamp(TIE,[L,H]) exactly, violations=0; 3×3 root L==H==9 TIE-invariant; L/H fingerprints bit-identical across TIE ∈ {0,±2,±16}); no single flat TIE reproduces the colour-symmetric (+2,−2) at 4×4 (analytic, bracket [1,16]/[−16,−1]).

Under aligned rules (basic ko, tie 0) weizigo fixpoint (+1) and MIGOS search (+1, thesis Table 5.1) agree, so the +1-vs-+2 gap is a ruleset (cycle-resolution) difference, not a fixpoint-vs-search discrepancy; candidate (b) (defect) is not needed to explain the gap, though our value for our game still awaits the #2 auditor.
